title: Streaming inference vendor contract playbook (working notes)
body:
Purpose
---
Quick working playbook for negotiating and documenting minimum contractual, evidence, and operational controls for vendors that provide streaming inference or long-running token-stream APIs (hosted or on-prem agents). This doc is intentionally pragmatic — capture what to ask for, fallback positions, and the lightweight evidence we should accept from vendors during procurement and ongoing assurance.

Scope / when to use this playbook
- Applies when we will route user queries (partial or complete) over a streamed connection (websocket/gRPC server-stream) or support long-running sessions with KV/prefix caches on vendor-managed infra.
- Not for batch-only inference vendors or pure embedding services (separate checklist).

Key risk themes to cover early
1) Residual data persistence in streaming buffers / KV caches (on-disk, in-memory snapshots, checkpointing).
2) Telemetry and debug logs containing PII or customer data during streaming.
3) Key management when encryption keys are used for caching or swap files.
4) Degraded-mode behavior (connection drops, fail-open) and how cached state is handled.
5) Evidence and proof-of-deletion: how vendor proves they removed ephemeral state on request.

Negotiation positions (preferred -> acceptable fallback)
- Preferred: Ephemeral streaming buffers and KV caches never touch persistent storage; if swap occurs, data is encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK) and automatically zeroized on session end.
- Acceptable fallback: Encrypted at rest with vendor-managed keys + documented retention window <= 24 hours + API to trigger immediate purge for named sessions.
- Minimum: Documented controls for retention period, encrypted at rest, and formal process for forensic review following a data incident.

Suggested contract clauses (editable snippets)
1) Definition: "Streaming Inference Session" means any connection where partial responses, intermediate prompts, or KV cache entries are persisted or maintained across multiple request/response boundaries for the purpose of subsequent inference.

2) Ephemeral Persistence & Deletion (sample language):
- Vendor shall ensure that all Streaming Inference Session state (including but not limited to request prefixes, intermediate activations, transient KV cache entries, and debug traces) is either: (a) held only in non-persistent memory and destroyed on session termination, or (b) if persisted to disk, encrypted using keys controlled by Customer and retained only for the period necessary for operational stability (not to exceed 24 hours), unless Customer expressly authorizes longer retention.
- Vendor shall provide an authenticated API endpoint enabling Customer-initiated purge of named Streaming Inference Session state within 4 hours of request.

3) Keys and Cryptography:
- For any persisted streaming state, encryption at rest must employ AES-256 or equivalent; keys used to encrypt customer-specific persisted state must be held in a KMS with audit logs and key-rotation capabilities.
- Preferred: Customer-managed keys (CMK) via vendor integration with Customer KMS (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Fallback: vendor-managed keys with documented separation of duties and key rotation cadence <= 90 days.

4) Telemetry & Debug Traces:
- Vendor shall classify telemetry into (a) system-only (no user payload), (b) redacted traces (only metadata+fingerprints), (c) full traces (may contain customer content).
- Full traces shall not be collected by default. If full traces are required for debugging, such traces will be collected only after Customer consent via the support ticket and retained no longer than 30 days unless Customer authorizes longer retention.

5) Incident Notification & Evidence Preservation:
- Vendor must notify Customer of any suspected unauthorized access affecting Streaming Inference Sessions within 24 hours, and provide an initial summary within 48 hours.
- Vendor must preserve forensic evidence (immutable logs) for at least 90 days following notification and make them available under NDA for Customer or mutually agreed third-party auditors.

6) Availability / SLA for streaming endpoints:
- Target: 99.95% uptime for streaming endpoints at the edge location(s) specified in Exhibit A, measured monthly.
- Credits: prorated credits starting when monthly availability < 99.95%; specific ladder to be negotiated.
- Degraded-mode obligations: Vendor must document fallback behavior (requeue, drop, partial results) and explicitly call out whether cached session state is preserved, truncated, or discarded during failover.

Evidence & acceptance matrix (what the vendor must deliver during onboarding and annual review)
- Operational artifact (onboard): Architecture diagram showing streaming flow and where ephemeral state lives (in-memory vs persisted).
- Technical evidence (onboard): Sample API call demonstrating session purge (curl example) and a test purge report for a dummy session id.
- Security artifact: KMS audit snapshot (last 90 days) or policy showing CMK integration. If vendor-managed keys, provide KMS admin separation matrix and key rotation logs.
- Pen-test evidence: scoped red-team report for streaming endpoints (OWASP ASVS-like), with remediation owners and dates.
- Telemetry sample: redacted debug trace sample and a list of telemetry categories.
- Deletion attestation: Quarterly statement signed by authorised vendor security officer attesting to purge capability and number of customer-initiated purges executed.

Scoring rubric for procurement (quick, for vendor team use)
- A (preferred): CMK + session purge API < 4 hours + no persistent disk by default + incident notif < 24h.
- B (acceptable): Vendor-managed KMS + purge API < 24 hours + encrypted at rest by default.
- C (conditional): Retention window > 24h but <= 7d; must include compensating controls (granular access logging, immutability, 3rd party audit).
- D (reject unless exceptional): No purge API, retention > 30d, telemetry includes full traces by default.

Operational playbook snippets (for SRE / SOC integration)
- Onboarding test plan (SRE): 1) Establish test streaming session. 2) Push ~100MB payload across sessions, confirm end-to-end latency profiles. 3) Trigger session purge via API, verify removal with vendor attestation and search of logs. 4) Simulate failover and verify documented behavior.
- Monitoring hooks: require exposure of token-level (or request-id-level) trace IDs in vendor logs so we can tie to our tracing. Agree on log retention TTL and sampling rate.

Negotiation redlines and fallbacks (notes-to-self)
- Redline: "Vendor shall not retain, sell, or otherwise use customer streaming payloads for model training or service improvement unless Customer provides explicit opt-in in writing."
- Fallback: Allow aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvement under a strict differential privacy/aggregation threshold and opt-out.

Open questions / TODOs
- Ask legal: acceptable wording for "ephemeral" vs "non-persistent" to make it enforceable without specifying implementation details. (JIRA-SEC-3121)
- Product: will we require CMK in all enterprise contracts or tier it by revenue? Need guidance from GTM/pricing.
- Compliance: map these requirements to SOC2 control IDs and ISO clauses for easier audit ask.

Quick negotiation cheat-sheet for AEs (2 lines each)
- If prospect demands no CMK: accept vendor-managed keys only after confirming purge API < 4h + audited key separation + 3rd party attestation.
- If customer requires on-prem private deployment: ensure playbook is operationalized in the on-prem runbook and include the same purge API contract (vendor must provide CLI).

Appendix: sample purge API pattern (implementation-agnostic)
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/purge  (auth: bearer + session-owner-id)
- Response: 202 Accepted (async purge) with status endpoint /v1/operations/{op_id} showing progress and final result timestamped and signed.
- Audit record: vendor provides signed JSON audit record containing session_id, timestamp, actor, and retention window applied.

Appendix: sample telemetry categories (for clause mapping)
- system-metric: cpu, memory, queue-latency (no user content)
- session-metadata: session-id, client-ip, region, model-version (no user content)
- debug-trace: intermediate activations, token-level payloads (sensitive)
- aggregated-usage: request counts, percentile latencies (safe for product telemetry)

Notes on evidence acceptance (practical)
- We will accept redacted traces for initial review but require a full trace in a sealed, limited-access environment for SOC2/contractual evidence if the vendor scores B or C and streaming is in scope.
- For smaller vendors: accept self-attestation plus live demo purge + recorded video showing purge API. Escalate to formal audit for >$X M ARR or enterprise customers.

References & related artifacts
- See CONFLUENCE-Streaming-Inference-Playbook for mapping to controls.
- Related JIRA: SEC-3121 (language draft).
